solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some US cabs are painted so, notes vagrant, park there

parts.words: Some US cabs are painted so
parts.note: New York taxis are famously painted yellow

indicators.note: a vagrant wanders about, so the letters of notes wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A guide to American sights: yellow cabs, wandering music, and a park to visit.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowstone is the famous US national park in Wyoming, an example of a park.

clue.text: Around 4th of January, see promoted diary, an item in Xmas sales

indicators.note: the reversed see is placed around the chosen letter of January
in a down clue, promoted means moved upwards, so the word is read bottom to top

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

indicators.note: asks for the fourth letter of the word January

parts.note: a log is a written record kept day by day

explanation.surface: A shopper's note about a diary being pushed in early January sales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' turns ELY into YLE, and 'Around' puts U, the fourth letter of January, inside it to give YULE.
explanation.definitionFit: A yule log, the chocolate cake or log burnt at Christmas, is a seasonal item on sale.

clue.text: Feature of cut hair

definitions.meaning: a cut is a canal, and canals have gated chambers for raising boats

explanation.surface: A hairdresser points out a feature of a haircut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' is an old word for a canal, not a haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: Canal chambers with gates and lengths of hair share the same plural word.

clue.text: Stunned to expose Liberal in something fishy

parts.note: to out someone is to expose them publicly

indicators.note: the letter for Liberal sits inside the fish

parts.note: a cod is a fish

explanation.surface: A political scandal: someone stunned at exposing a Liberal caught up in shady dealings.
explanation.definitionFit: Being knocked out cold means being unconscious, as if stunned by a blow.

clue.text: Equestrian gear, with son taking over reins, initially agitates

indicators.note: the letter for son takes the place of the other letter in the gear word

parts.note: a stirrup is the foot support hung from a saddle

indicators.note: points to the first letter of reins

explanation.surface: Riding tack where a son takes the reins and gets a horse worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking over' swaps the R of STIRRUP, from 'reins initially', for S.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir up trouble or feelings is to agitate them.

clue.text: Pensioner eats very loudly with those people in a faraway location

indicators.note: the pensioner's letters take the other pieces inside, as if swallowing them

parts.note: OAP is old-age pensioner
ff (fortissimo) is the musical mark for very loud
them refers to those people

explanation.surface: A noisy pensioner eating with some others in a remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: OAP (old-age pensioner) is a British term for a retired person.
explanation.definitionFit: Somewhere off the map is so remote it does not appear on charts: an idiom for far away.

clue.text: War victim perhaps advanced signal during the night before

indicators.note: the pieces come in the middle of the night before, inside it

parts.note: eve is the evening before a day
A is an abbreviation for advanced, as in A level
a cue is a signal to act

explanation.surface: A wartime warning given in the dead of night before something happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks an example: children sent from British cities in WWII were the classic evacuees.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moved away from danger in wartime is an example of a person affected by war.

clue.text: Copper receives shout of approval, and thanks, retrieving furry animal

indicators.note: the policeman's letters take in the shout

parts.note: a copper is a police constable, PC
ole is the Spanish cry of approval

indicators.note: retrieving suggests bringing back, so the word for thanks is read backwards

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A police officer, cheered and thanked, rescues a pet animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The polecat is a weasel-like mammal with thick dark fur.

clue.text: Some of chicken put forward to circumvent burning tin

indicators.note: to circumvent is to go around, so the outer word goes around the others

parts.note: to pose a question is to put it forward
arson is deliberate burning
Sn is the chemical symbol for tin

explanation.surface: A cooking mishap: chicken pushed ahead to avoid a burning tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The fatty rump of a cooked bird is jokingly called by this name, a part of a chicken.

clue.text: Make red wine, leaving one week and drinking … extremely frail in morning

indicators.note: the shortened wine takes in the other pieces as if drinking them
the letter for one week leaves the word wine

parts.note: taken as written
W is the abbreviation for week

indicators.note: points to the outer letters of frail

explanation.surface: A morning hangover: someone very frail drinking red wine, a week on.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis is only for the surface; 'in' is a link word, and the shortened wine, INE, holds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To inflame skin or a wound is to make it hot, swollen and reddened.

clue.text: Making uniform go with new dress

parts.note: evening means making level or uniform

explanation.surface: A fashion tip: smoothing out a new outfit and wearing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A long formal gown worn at night is a kind of dress.

clue.text: Car manufacturer functions noisily

indicators.note: noisily says the word is to be heard, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: roles are functions or jobs

explanation.surface: A car maker whose engines work loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for Rolls-Royce, the British maker of luxury motor cars.

clue.text: Modelling shoot involves a purpose for brewery building

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in the a
modelling is shaping, so the letters of shoot are moulded into a new order

parts.note: a use is a purpose

explanation.surface: A modelling photo shoot staged with a purpose at a brewery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modelling' rearranges SHOOT as OSTHO, and 'involves' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiln for drying hops, found in Kent, serves the brewing trade.

clue.text: Vigilant, rung a crook getting into overdraft

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the abbreviation

parts.note: OD is the abbreviation for overdrawn or overdraft

indicators.note: crook as an adjective means bent or unwell, so the letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: A villain who rings for help while sliding into debt must stay alert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone standing ready for danger is watchful: an idiom for being alert.

clue.text: Late joiner entering mainly on the lookout for old ruler

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the shortened word
mainly means most of it, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: alert means on the lookout
ex means former or late
and is a joining word

explanation.surface: A latecomer joining a watch party for an old monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Late' means former here, not tardy, and 'joiner' is a conjunction rather than a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander the Great was the ancient Macedonian king and conqueror.

clue.text: Ceremonial area around Leytonstone where things once erupted

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial display
E11 is the London postcode district for Leytonstone, with the digits read as two letters I

explanation.surface: A grand ceremony in an east London district where things once boiled over.
explanation.walkthrough: Leytonstone is a district of east London; its postcode E11 reads as EII.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman city was buried when Vesuvius erupted in AD 79.

clue.text: Weather feature they broadcast about mouth of Humber

indicators.note: the sowers word goes about the letter

parts.note: sowers broadcast seed by scattering it

indicators.note: mouth of means the first letter, the opening of the word Humber

explanation.surface: A forecast about rain at the Humber estuary, read out on air.
explanation.walkthrough: The Humber is an estuary in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Brief falls of rain are a familiar weather feature.

clue.text: Captain literally raised boxing dukes before onset of the scrap

indicators.note: the reversed name boxes in the dukes
in a down clue, raised means read from the bottom up

parts.note: Captain Nemo of Jules Verne; nemo is Latin for no one, so his name is taken literally as written
D is the abbreviation for duke, so two dukes give two Ds

indicators.note: onset is the start, the first letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A captain raising his fists before a fight begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' gives OMEN; 'dukes' looks like slang for fists but is two dukes; 'scrap' looks like a fight but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftover fragment of cloth or food is a small scrap.

clue.text: Odds on house number 15 causing this?

parts.note: SP is starting price, the odds in a race
a lodge is a small house

explanation.surface: A betting question about odds on a particular house number.
explanation.walkthrough: Number 15 is the answer to 15 across, rain showers, which may leave a splash of mud or water.
explanation.definitionFit: Rain may leave a blot or smear, cleverly defined by what causes it.

clue.text: Henry VIII perhaps gobbles one platter, repulsing poet

indicators.note: the king's letters swallow the other pieces

parts.note: Henry VIII is an example of a king
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: repulsing means pushing back, so the record's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a platter is slang for a record, an LP

explanation.surface: Henry VIII wolfing down a plateful, which drives off a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling wrote If and many other verses, so he counts as a poet.

clue.text: Important women fly back, half missing US resort

parts.note: key means important

indicators.note: back says the fly's name is read backwards
with half missing, only the first half of the letters remains

parts.note: the tsetse is an African fly

explanation.surface: Key women take a flight back to an American resort, half of them absent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half missing' keeps one half of the fly's name, TSE, and 'back' turns it into EST.
explanation.definitionFit: The island city at the tip of the Florida Keys is a holiday resort.

clue.text: Aversion one shows with lines written by Shakespeare?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L stands for line, so two Ls are lines
Will is Shakespeare's first name

explanation.surface: Someone showing distaste for verses penned by the Bard.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostility or enmity toward someone is a strong dislike, an aversion.

clue.text: Reprinted bold top line where sentence begins?

indicators.note: printed again means the letters of bold are set in a new order

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, top, with the 1 read as I
a ley is a straight line linking ancient sites

explanation.surface: A printer resets a heading in bold to start a sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sentence' is a court sentence, not grammar: the Old Bailey is London's Central Criminal Court.
explanation.definitionFit: Criminals are sentenced at London's main criminal court, where a prison term starts.

clue.text: Slovak, out of position, misses final volley

indicators.note: the letters are displaced into a new order
the last letter of Slovak is left out

explanation.surface: A Slovak player out of position misses the last shot of a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misses final' drops K from SLOVAK, and 'out of position' rearranges SLOVA.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a burst of gunfire or a barrage, a volley.

clue.text: A bit of honesty liberated old writers

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase gives a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A touch of honesty set free some old authors.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointed tools for writing on wax tablets were used in ancient times.

clue.text: Staff surrounded by journalist, then another, corrected errors

indicators.note: the staff word goes inside the journalist's letters

parts.note: ED is an editor, a journalist
staff are the men of a workforce
another journalist, a second ED

explanation.surface: Staff ringed by one journalist after another, fixing mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text is to remove its mistakes, so emended means corrected.

clue.text: Spiritual side to yoga is back in style

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the style word

parts.note: elan is flair or style

indicators.note: the first side, the opening letter of yoga
the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: A yoga class's spiritual aspect is fashionable again.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the Elysian Fields, the Greek paradise, hence heavenly or blissful.

clue.text: They're regularly applying research to test earth-dweller

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

parts.note: res is short for research
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: Scientists apply research findings in a test.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrestrial is a being living on land or on the planet, as opposed to an alien.
